Fire Block Materials

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Fire blocks are of materials that remain in place and
prevent the passage of flames for not less than 15 min
When subjected to the standard fire exposure in
CAN/ULC-S101. Except as permitted by Sentences (2) and (3).
Fire blocks are deemed to comply with Sentence (1) if
they are constructed of not less than
(a) 0.38 mm (0.015″) sheet steel, (b) 12.7 mm (½″) gypsum
board, (c) 12.5 mm (½″) plywood, OSB or waferboard, with
joints having continuous supports, (d) two layers of lumber,
each not less than 19 mm (¾″) thick, with joints staggered,
or (e) 38 mm (1½″) lumber.
In a building permitted to be of combustible
construction, semi-rigid fibre insulation board of
glass, rock or slag may block the vertical space in a
double-frame wall at a floor
Where the space is not over 25 mm (1″) wide and the board
(a) has a density not less than 45 kg/m³ (2.8 lb/ft³), (b)
is securely fastened to one set of studs, (c) extends from
below the bottom of the top plates in the lower storey to
above the top of the bottom plate in the upper storey, and
(d) completely fills the portion of the vertical space
between the headers and between the wall plates. See Note
The figure in the Note shows where the board goes at the
intersection of walls and floors in wood-frame construction.
It illustrates the fire block detail, not a design of a fire
separation.
Drawn: red outlines are the fire blocks. In B the insulation board is yellow, the near wall stops part way.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.16.3. (page 9-93)
